system: You read a chat transcript about a fictional workstation and list durable technical claims. Reply as JSON: c is a list of [user, claim, refs], refs being the transcript line numbers that support the claim.
transcript:
[1] member-a1b2: Finally cracked the Quanta 40 case after thirty years of hoarding it.
[2] member-c3d4: Nice! Still booting off the cartridge slot or did you swap the boot ROM?
[3] member-a1b2: Jumper J7 selects the boot ROM source; I set it to the flash chip on the daughterboard.
[4] member-e5f6: Watch J7, it is a 3-pin and pins 2-3 are ROM mode, pins 1-2 are cartridge.
[5] member-c3d4: The cooling fan on mine died. Was it the 12V axial or the 5V one?
[6] member-a1b2: Definitely the 12V fan behind the CPU heatsink; replaced it with a 12V unit.
[7] member-e5f6: While you are in there, C42 near the power rail is bulging, swap it for a 100uF/16V.
[8] member-c3d4: Great call, that electrolytic was leaking. Report back once it POSTs!

reviews.claim: On the Quanta 40, jumper J7 selects the boot ROM source.
Quanta 40 jumper J7 pins 2-3 select ROM mode and pins 1-2 select the cartridge.
The Quanta 40 cooling fan behind the CPU heatsink runs at 12V.
Capacitor C42 near the Quanta 40 power rail is 100uF/16V.
The Quanta 40 ships with a removable GPU card.
The Quanta 40 case was opened after thirty years.
